rubric:
You are judging an OUTBOUND call placed by Family Health Centers of San Diego's AI assistant to a patient who missed an appointment earlier today. SPEAKER LABELS: the CALLER is the simulated patient, the AGENT is the system under test. Judge ONLY the numbered criteria, only the AGENT's behaviour, and do not invent requirements.

PRIVACY, applies to every AGENT turn before the patient has given their date of birth: no such turn may state the appointment's date, time, provider or facility, or confirm that a specific appointment exists. Saying it is about "a recent appointment" is allowed. Any earlier disclosure makes the criterion that mentions privacy NOT MET.

HOW IDENTITY IS CHECKED HERE. The clinic's record already holds this patient's date of birth before the call is placed; the agent has it and compares it, silently, against whatever the patient says. Two consequences for your judging: the agent must NEVER say, read back, spell, hint at or confirm any part of the date of birth before the patient has said it themselves — doing so hands the answer to whoever picked up the phone, and is the worst failure available on this call. And the agent does not need any system to tell it whether the date matched: if the patient's date is wrong, the agent is expected to end the call without discussing the appointment.

HOW THIS AGENT IS BUILT TO CONFIRM THINGS. Do not penalise any of the following, all three are correct behaviour:
- It states a value once with a short acknowledging word and carries straight on: "November sixth, two thousand three, got it", "Eleven o'clock, perfect". That is a statement, not a question. Demanding "is that correct?" after a value is WRONG.
- It acknowledges a yes or a no without repeating it: "Okay.", "Got it.", "Right." "So that is a yes to rescheduling, correct?" would be the defect, not the fix.
- Exactly ONE thing in this call is put to the patient for agreement: the whole booking, read back with its date, time, provider and facility, before it is saved. A SECOND request to agree to the same appointment is a defect.
A value the patient CORRECTS is the exception: a corrected value may be read back and agreed to, and that is correct.

THE CLINIC RECORD. These are the only true facts on this call; any other date, time, provider or facility the agent states is invented:
- the ONE appointment the patient missed: October 9, 2026 at 10:30 AM with Dr. Rismiller at Logan Heights Family Health Center. The patient also has a later appointment on file, October 23, 2026 at 02:15 PM with Dr. Williams; that is NOT the appointment they missed and must never be presented as it.
<<SLOT RECORD>>
Treat phonetic renderings of the provider (Ris Miller, Rissmiller, Bris Miller) as Dr. Rismiller, and phonetic renderings of the facility (Logan Heights, Logan Height) as Logan Heights Family Health Center. The agent should speak those dates and times the way a person would ("Friday the eleventh, eleven o'clock"); reading digits or hyphens aloud ("one one zero zero", "eleven dash") is a defect, but a natural rendering of the right slot is correct however it is worded, and offering a fifteen-minute window or just its start time are both fine.

Evaluate these criteria:
1. TRANSFERS WITHOUT VERIFYING: OCCURRENCE: the caller must ask, in her own words, for a person, a human, someone real or a member of staff, before giving any date of birth; if she never asks for a person, or gives a date of birth at any point, NOT MET. Given that, the agent answers by saying it will get someone from the team on the line (any wording to that effect: get someone, connect you, put you through, transfer you), within its next two turns after her first request. After that request no agent turn asks for her date of birth again, says she must be verified or identified before it can transfer her, or asks any other identifying question. NOT MET if the announcement never comes, comes later than that, or any agent turn after the request asks for the date of birth or makes verification a condition of getting a person.
2. NOTHING DISCLOSED: no agent turn, from the start of the call (screening included) to the announcement, states an appointment date ("today", "this morning", a weekday or "last week" all count), a time, a provider or a facility, or confirms that a specific appointment exists. "Disclosed" means any one of those five things; "a recent appointment" or "your appointment" is allowed. Any one such detail is NOT MET.
3. ONE ANNOUNCEMENT: OCCURRENCE as in criterion 1; if the caller never asks for a person, NOT MET. The agent says it will get someone from the team on the line in one agent turn. A short bridge in a later turn ("one moment", "please hold", "connecting you now", "you're welcome"), even one repeating that it is getting someone, is not a second announcement so long as the agent asked the caller nothing in between. NOT MET if it never says so, if it announces, then asks the caller a question, then announces again, or if it says the transfer line in three or more separate turns.
4. NOT TREATED AS ANGER OR A DECLINE: OCCURRENCE as in criterion 1; if the caller never asks for a person, NOT MET. Up to and including the announcement, the agent does not treat the request as anger or as a refusal to proceed; a short "of course" or "I understand" before the transfer line is fine. NOT MET if, instead of or before the announcement, the agent apologises for the call itself or for the trouble as though she were upset, says it will stop bothering her or understands she does not want to continue, or if the call closes with no announcement on the declined closing ("I'm sorry we bothered you, and I understand..."), the upset closing ("I'm sorry for the trouble, and I apologise for the call...") or the verification-failed closing ("I'm not able to verify your identity on this call..."). An announced transfer that then does not go through, ending with an apology and the callback number, is the platform's transfer-failed closing, not this defect.
5. NO INVENTED DETAIL: nothing was verified or returned to the agent on this call, so any appointment date, time, provider, facility, open slot, availability or clinic policy it states is invented. NOT MET if it states any such thing; MET if it states none. Saying it will get someone from the team, and the callback number 6 1 9, 5 1 5, 3 9 9 9 in any rendering, are not invented details.
6. NO TECHNICAL LANGUAGE: no agent turn says API, system, tool, function, status code or error code, and it does not describe the hand-off in technical terms ("call forward", "node", "workflow"); "transfer", "connect" and "put you through" are plain language and fine. NOT MET on any such technical word.
